newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Bank of Slovenia sees no change in monetary policy.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Slovenia sees no change in monetary policy.

text.p: Bank of Slovenia governor France Arhar said on Wednesday there will be no change in Slovenian monetary policy this year despite exporters' claims that the strength of the tolar is hampering trade.
"Our goal is to keep a stable currency," Arhar said in a speech to financiers.
"We can best help the economy through a stable currency. Lower inflation means greater savings and those are a precondition for investment," he added.
Arhar said the bank had no intention of devaluing the tolar, which is currently quoted at 91.28 to the mark, compared to 91.00 at the start of 1997 and 88.00 at the start of 1996.
Annual inflation in March eased to 7.4 percent from 8.8 percent at the end of 1996. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
